Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category endowed with a topology $J$.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $S$ be a sieve on $U$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The sieve $S$ is a covering sieve.
\item The sheafification $S^\# \to h_U^\#$
of the map $S \to h_U$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
stage_b_substantive_review_note: Independent comparison against pinned original theorem in Stage A sites.tex:11685; no proof or unsafe raw slice viewed. For a sieve S⊆h_U, being covering is equivalent to its sheafification S#→h_U# being an isomorphism. The source's equivalence and the precise comparison morphism are preserved; both properties are symmetrically searchable.

stage_a_original_draft:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $J$, $J'$ be topologies on $\mathcal{C}$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $J = J'$,
\item sheaves for the topology $J$ are the same as
sheaves for the topology $J'$.
\end{enumerate}
stage_b_substantive_review_note: Independent comparison against pinned original theorem in Stage A sites.tex:11734; no proof or unsafe raw slice viewed. A Grothendieck topology on the same category is determined by the class of set sheaves it defines. Equality of J,J' iff equality of their sheaf categories is the exact original biconditional, not mere inclusion.

\label{lemma-finer-topology}
Assumption and notation as in Theorem \ref{theorem-topology-and-topos}.
Then $J \subset J'$ if and only if every sheaf for the
topology $J'$ is a sheaf for the topology $J$.
